title: The Metal That Remembers
hook: Your eyeglasses frames might be made of a metal that remembers.
script: Your eyeglasses frames might be made of a metal that remembers. What if you could crumple a paperclip and have it heal itself? Ordinary steel permanently bends after a tiny zero point two percent strain. But a shape memory alloy called nitinol can be stretched eight percent and still recover. It doesn't slide atoms; it simply reorients its crystal structure like a folding piece of paper. This is why nitinol returns to shape the instant you add heat. Some versions trigger at exactly thirty-seven degrees Celsius. This allows tiny stents to stay chilled and flexible until they warm up inside your artery. It's a material that behaves less like a mineral and more like a living thing.
